summary: 14-day Nightscout analysis demonstrates excellent overall glycemic control with an average glucose of 117.0 mg/dL, 99.7% Time in Range (70-180 mg/dL), 0.0% time below 70 mg/dL, and low glycemic variability (CV 12.9%). Active AAPS profile parameters (basal rates, CR, ISF, DIA) and oref1 automation settings are well-calibrated. Postprandial rises following weekend brunch reach 188 mg/dL at 2 hours but resolve completely to target within 4 hours without late hypoglycemia.
strengths: Time in Range is exceptionally high at 99.7% with zero recorded episodes below 70 mg/dL across 14 days.
Overnight glucose remains stable between 102 and 112 mg/dL across all target segments.
Glycemic variability is low with a standard deviation of 15.1 mg/dL and coefficient of variation of 12.9%.
Continuous glucose monitor coverage is complete at 100% with no data gaps over the 14-day audit window.
issues: Weekend brunch exhibits a 2-hour postprandial peak reaching 188 mg/dL (+62 to +70 mg/dL rise) before returning to baseline by 4 hours.
Weekday breakfast shows a consistent 2-hour postprandial rise up to 157-167 mg/dL before smoothly recovering by 240 minutes.
AAPS raw export has unpopulated (null) fields for specific conditional SMB toggles and explicit Autosens state indicators.
education: Time in Range above 70% with less than 4% below range represents international target guidance for automated insulin delivery.
Postprandial spikes that resolve within 3 to 4 hours without causing late hypoglycemia indicate appropriate Carb Ratio (CR) and Duration of Insulin Action (DIA) settings.
Extended carbohydrates (e-carbs) in oref1 model delayed absorption over time rather than delivering a pump extended bolus, allowing SMB and UAM to safely match high-fat or mixed meals.
safety_notes: Decision-support content only. The user must independently verify every proposed change, make changes one at a time, and monitor glucose closely.
Always consult with your clinical care team before adjusting active basal rates, insulin sensitivity factors, or safety limits.
Ensure hypoglycemia treatment guidelines are reviewed and rapid-acting carbohydrates are readily available whenever testing profile adjustments.

recommendations.title: Optimize Weekend Brunch Prebolus Timing
recommendations.description: Weekend brunch shows a 2-hour postprandial peak reaching 188 mg/dL before returning to baseline by 4 hours. Extending prebolus timing from 10 minutes to 15-20 minutes or increasing immediate bolus percentage from 60% to 70% can flatten this rise without changing underlying profile parameters.

recommendations.title: Verify Handheld Device SMB and Sensitivity Settings
recommendations.description: Exported profile data contains null values for specific conditional SMB activation flags and explicit Autosens toggles. Verify on the handheld AndroidAPS device UI that desired SMB conditions and sensitivity settings are configured as intended.

meal_strategy_summary.suggestion: Maintain current 15-20 minute prebolus timing and 70% immediate bolus with active SMB/UAM for routine meals. For higher-fat/higher-carb weekend brunch, consider extending prebolus timing to 15-20 minutes to reduce the 2-hour peak while keeping total carbs and e-carb settings unchanged.
meal_strategy_summary.rationale: Weekday breakfast and dinner demonstrate excellent postprandial resolution within 3-4 hours. Weekend brunch achieves full 4-hour recovery but exhibits a transient 2-hour peak at 188 mg/dL.
meal_strategy_summary.next_observation: Log exact prebolus duration and meal start times for weekend brunch to confirm whether the 120-minute rise is due to prebolus timing lag or fat/protein absorption delay.

exceptions.suggestion: Extend prebolus timing from 10 minutes to 15-20 minutes or increase immediate bolus share from 60% to 70%.
exceptions.rationale: Peak glucose reaches 188 mg/dL at 120 minutes but recovers completely to 115 mg/dL at 240 minutes, indicating adequate total insulin but slightly delayed insulin action onset relative to carb absorption.

implementation_steps: Step 1: Continue running current active profile parameters (basal, CR, ISF, DIA) and AAPS safety limits without making device adjustments.
Step 2: Verify specific conditional SMB activation toggles on the AndroidAPS handheld UI to ensure exported null fields match your desired device setup.
Step 3: On the next weekend brunch, trial a 15-minute prebolus (instead of 10 minutes) while leaving total carbohydrate entries and insulin doses unchanged.
Step 4: Monitor glucose response at 1 and 2 hours post-brunch to evaluate if peak excursion is attenuated.
Step 5: Review overall 14-day Time in Range and glucose trends after 4 weeks.
